Stop spending months rewriting entire applications in Rust just to fix a few slow functions. 🚀

Most performance bottlenecks live in less than 5 percent of your codebase. Instead of burning time on a full-stack rewrite, you can now profile your high-level app, let AI agents surgically port only the hottest spots to Rust, and drop them right back in.

EL4CTEO/fast-anything is a hybrid performance optimization tool that brings native execution speed to Python, Node, TypeScript, Ruby, PHP, Go, and more without forcing you to abandon your core architecture.

Key features include:
⚡ Broad Polyglot Support: Works seamlessly across Python, Node, TS, Ruby, Java, Go, PHP, C/C++, C#, and R.
🔍 Automated Correctness Verification: Records real production calls, derives rigorous edge cases and shrunk inputs, and guarantees strict parity before enabling any Rust port.
🤖 AI Coding Agent Integration: Built-in support for Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and tools like Claude Code to automate the entire porting loop via a single CLI command.
📦 Minimalist Compilation: Compiles single-function Rust crates sharing a common dependency cache, entirely avoiding massive target directory bloat.

Achieve up to 100x speedups on data-intensive text processing, fuzzy deduplication loops, and CPU-bound math algorithms while keeping your sanity intact. 

Check out the repo and accelerate your bottlenecks today:
https://github.com/EL4CTEO/fast-anything

Tired of AI coding assistants wasting your token quotas and dragging down your workflow with sluggish, turn-by-turn tool executions? 

Meet agy-fast: a specialized local MCP accelerator plugin for Google Antigravity that slashes LLM turns by over 33 percent, cuts token quotas, and eliminates costly wall-clock latency through batched operations and instant workspace snapshots.

The Problem:
AI agents working inside Google Antigravity environments often hit heavy rate-limiting bottlenecks and run up massive bills because they waste time and tokens on repetitive, fragmented search, multi-file edits, and exploration turns. 

The Solution:
agy-fast aggregates these high-frequency operations into a persistent, zero-dependency local Model Context Protocol server. It injects a lightweight workspace snapshot at session startup and processes multi-step actions locally in batches, drastically reducing round-trip token overhead without altering native UI components.

Notable Features:
- Persistent local Stdio Model Context Protocol server that batches up to 20 code searches, 50 file edits, or 12 build commands into single execution rounds.
- Session start hook that injects a sub-50ms, highly compact workspace snapshot containing git state, directory structure, and script configs.
- Zero-dependency, pre-built ECMAScript module architecture requiring no external runtime installations beyond Node.js.
- Built-in offline performance benchmarking utilities that analyze JSONL interaction transcripts to measure token savings.

Perfect for large-scale multi-file refactoring, cutting token costs during intensive debugging, and boosting your overall agent task velocity in Antigravity.

Check out the repo and start accelerating your workflow today:
https://github.com/INK-Q/agy-fast

The Lean theorem prover community is formally verifying a 2026 proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, pushing interactive mathematics to the bleeding edge. 🚀

Mathematics relies on absolute truth, but handling massive, bleeding-edge proofs often leaves room for human error. This project provides a community-driven Lean formalization and maintenance effort for a 2026 proof of the Riemann Hypothesis and the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, ensuring machine-checked mathematical validity via strict kernel verification.

Whether you are a formal mathematician, type theorist, or software engineer interested in automated reasoning, here is what is under the hood:

✨ Machine-checked proof verification of the Riemann Hypothesis and related Dirichlet L-function theorems using Lean 4 and Mathlib.
🔒 A custom comparator infrastructure that validates theorems against clean challenge statements with zero unauthorized axioms.
🛡️ Sandboxed compilation and export tools designed to safely run, export, and cross-verify untrusted mathematical submissions.
⚡ Performance-optimized caching workflows enabling developers to inspect and build complex formal proofs without requiring massive local compute resources.

For developers working in formal verification, this repository serves as a high-profile blueprint for organizing, refactoring, and optimizing massive computational proof trees. You can use it to study advanced interactive theorem proving patterns and large-scale project modularity in Lean 4, or to audit high-stakes mathematical proofs using cryptographic export comparisons and isolated kernel checking environments.

👉 Check out the repository and explore the codebase here:
https://github.com/leanprover-community/riemann-hypothesis

Tired of Electron-based apps eating up your RAM just to watch a video? 

Meet Stream Tube, a high-performance native YouTube client built in Rust using GPUI, featuring zero bloat and native integrations for SponsorBlock, DeArrow, and Return YouTube Dislike. 

🔥 The Problem Solved:
Browser-based YouTube viewing is notorious for resource-heavy overhead, intrusive ads, and UI clutter. Stream Tube bypasses the browser entirely, offering a lightweight, GPU-accelerated native desktop client designed for Windows and Linux that puts performance and privacy first.

⚡ Key Features:
- GPU-accelerated native UI built with Rust and the GPUI framework for minimal RAM usage and buttery-smooth rendering.
- Direct video stream playback via libmpv combined with native integrations for SponsorBlock, DeArrow, and Return YouTube Dislike.
- Comprehensive privacy controls supporting local-only subscriptions or optional Google sign-in with SQLite-backed history and yt-dlp downloading.
- Deep customization including audio-only mode, UI density scaling, proxy support, and browser integration via custom URI schemes and userscripts.

🛠️ Why Developers Should Care:
If you are a Rust engineer interested in GUI programming, this codebase is an incredible real-world reference implementation. Study it to learn advanced GPUI patterns and state management, how to integrate media playback engines like libmpv, handle local SQLite databases, and structure complex native desktop utilities.

👉 Check out the repo and drop a star:
https://github.com/Avaneesh-Inamdar/Stream-Tube-Desktop

🔊 What if your trackpad could talk? 

Meet `nospeaker`—a wild open-source project that turns your MacBook haptic trackpad into an actual acoustic speaker by driving its motor up to 4,000 times a second! 🤯

💻 The Problem:
Laptops have built-in speakers, but what if you want to experiment with unconventional hardware actuation, or need low-level audio-tactile feedback where traditional speakers aren't ideal? Apple’s public haptic APIs won't let you do this, leaving the trackpad strictly for clicks and gentle bumps.

⚙️ How it works:
nospeaker bypasses public APIs entirely, directly invoking undocumented functions in the private macOS MultitouchSupport framework. By passing custom frequency, strength, and length dictionaries to the trackpad motor, it transforms the solid glass surface into a vibrating speaker capable of speech, singing, and frequency sweeps.

🚀 Key Features:
• Real-Time Voice Synthesis: Samples macOS built-in text-to-speech, extracts formants every 10 milliseconds via linear prediction, and maps them to dual-tone haptic frequencies.
• Zero-Dependency Architecture: Contained entirely within a single Swift file that builds natively for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.
• Flexible Routing: Supports custom text input, voice selection, and external Magic Trackpad routing.
• Low-Level Mastery: A masterclass in reverse-engineering macOS peripheral drivers and handling real-time digital signal processing.

Whether you are building novel accessibility tools, silent haptic notification systems, or just love hacking low-level OS internals, this repository is an incredible playground for systems engineers and hardware hackers. 

👉 Check out the code and try it out on your Mac:
https://github.com/os6/nospeaker
